observation_kind: 56 official source facts cross-validated in four modes plus 10 exact-data blockers; not 234 independent HTTP fetches
m: Official page content was read back.
The fact is consistent with the published source contract.
The fact was applied as a fail-closed guard to the three preserved candidates.
Source URL, publisher role and reuse/provenance requirements were retained.
f: Current INSPIRE publication date is 5 July 2026.
New INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
London Borough of Haringey is listed in the current download index.
INSPIRE polygons are separated into local-authority files.
The downloadable polygon format is GML.
A GIS is required to view the downloaded polygons.
The dataset is reusable under the Open Government Licence.
The dataset is a subset of registered freehold land and property.
Polygons show indicative position and extent rather than definitive legal extent.
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry INSPIRE ID.
The individual title plan is required to establish registered extent.
Polygon coordinates are captured against the British National Grid.
British National Grid is represented as EPSG:27700 in the workflow.
BNG-to-WGS84 conversion may shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets.
Latitude and longitude can query entities whose geometry intersects a point.
A coordinate request can contain multiple dataset parameters.
Responses can include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point.
No result does not prove that no constraint exists because coverage varies.
Coordinate and custom query geometry use WGS84.
Spatial filters support within, intersects, contains and related predicates.
Responses can provide next, previous, first and last pagination links.
The property-screening API has no batch endpoint.
Bulk downloads support CSV, JSON and where applicable GeoJSON and Parquet.
Article 4 area reports 7,152 records, 112 providers and 31 July 2026 freshness.
Article 4 direction reports 3,175 records, 102 providers and 31 July 2026 freshness.
Article 4 publishing requires direction and direction-area datasets.
Article 4 area geometry is polygon or multipolygon in WGS84.
The composite 1m DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The composite has one metre spatial resolution.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser return.
Surface objects are removed to produce a terrain-only model.
The current composite was produced in 2022.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Repeated coverage uses the newest best-resolution survey.
Composite surveys span 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km OS National Grid tiles.
Heights are metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
Input survey vertical accuracy is plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The dataset coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features services are listed.
The current OS Terrain 50 version date is July 2026.
The product covers all of Great Britain.
The product is free OpenData under the Open Government Licence.
OS Terrain 50 is a bare-earth digital terrain model.
The product is updated annually in July.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
Tiled supplies use 10km by 10km National Grid tiles.
Tile identifiers quote the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
The grid uses regular 50 metre post spacing.
Grid data is supplied as ASCII grid with accompanying GML metadata.
A 10km tile contains 200 pixels per row and 200 rows.
Height values represent pixel centres; rows run west-east and progress south.
ASCII height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
OpenData API operations need no API key and support TQ area filtering plus 200/307 responses.
